errors.what: Identity-collapse diagnosis was read off a stale uninitialised variable captured inside spawn_from, which only runs when the spawn bar is met, so it printed its initialiser
'1 of 4096 used' was a 32-EVAL-WINDOW probe, not run utilization; misread as catastrophic routing concentration for ~10 turns and four failed fixes were built on it
rerun.sh parallel gate: $JOBS used in the banner before it was defined; set -u killed the gate in 2s
grep -c exits non-zero when the count is 0, so `|| echo 1` fired on top of grep's own '0' and tb became the two-line string '0\n1' -- every arm reported FAIL
IndexError in the new ROUTER SELECTION line when fab.use is empty (_uv[0] on an empty list)
use[] was written only on the society path, so under SOCIETY=0 the utilization table stayed empty and culling, the breadth cap and discovery were all silently disabled on every chaining run ever made
Uploaded smoke-log zip was empty: 182 bytes, one directory entry, 0 bytes uncompressed. Gate result unverifiable
SUFFICIENCY section has printed nothing since routing went per-window: int(_os[j]) applied to a whole row raised ValueError straight into the section's own except clause

Fabric._ids cached graph-attached tensors -- a cache hit would backward through a freed graph; it never fired only because the training loop never passed step=, so the full O(N*2dr*hid) embed ran every step at N=4096
prompt.py chaining branch did `_h = FAB(...)`, assigning the whole 4-tuple and handing it to model.head -- guaranteed TypeError the instant a chaining checkpoint was sampled
prompt.py took the forward path from the environment rather than the checkpoint, so a society-trained checkpoint would generate as a chain once the default moved

FAB_EMB_EVERY defaulted to 50 and was a GRADIENT switch, not a cache cadence -- live on chaining (passes step=) and dead on society, throttling the only channel reaching the whole population to 1 step in 50 and routing on keys up to 50 steps stale
halt_b was allocated, optimized, weight-decayed and never gradiented on the chaining path -- the path made default one commit earlier

LM training curve verdict read its own sign backwards: _d8 is prev-current so negative means the loss ROSE, yet the text asserted 'still FALLING' regardless of sign, and it only compared the last two points

Config banner printed environment values rather than effective values -- a whole 48k-step SOCIETY=0 run logged 'per-expert memory ON' while MEM_PER_EXPERT was `... and SOCIETY` and therefore off from step 0. WORLD_GROW had the same shape
UnboundLocalError: banner referenced WORLD_MODEL before assignment

route_w (society) and Fabric.forward (chaining) each had their own entry router and had drifted: chaining used free learned q_entry keys with no region term and no centroid update anywhere, while the banner reported 'grounded region + learned bilinear'
A mechanical dedent while extracting entry_logits mangled the file into an IndentationError

Cadence bug, 4 instances: `step % MANAGE_EVERY == 0` never coincides with a batch-flush step at BATCH_W=4, so GRADIENT REACH, ROUTING MIX, CHAIN ORDER and maybe_deepen never fired. maybe_deepen's non-execution invalidated a reported result
SyntaxError in the rewritten ROUTING banner: missing `+` after a parenthesised conditional inside the f-string concatenation; killed all three arms
dom_ban was computed in the society branch and never passed to forward(), so the percentage breadth cap the researcher asked for was inert on the chaining path the whole time

The growth ramp never latched off: armed while `n < ramp_to * cap`, and culling holds n just under the cap forever, so it re-fired every ~187 steps for entire runs. 10062 grown = ~4093 building the population once + ~5969 refilling culls; the population was replaced ~1.5x over
longrun.sh grid hardcoded WIN/BATCH_W/ENC_WARMUP so toy overrides did not apply; a verification run spent 2000 encoder warmup steps on CPU and timed out
The append-only unique-name helper written into longrun.sh had a malformed glob (produced a-2.log/a-3.log incorrectly)
DIV_W was a local of main() and invisible to Fabric.forward -- NameError on the first chaining hop that would have killed 15 of the 18 grid arms

Society DIV_W indexed _O (rank-ordered) with a global expert id -> IndexError. Un-runnable since routing went per-window, so the one term rewarding experts for differing had never once been on in a real run
Dead module-level ROUTE_T = _f('ROUTE_T', 1.0): assigned, never read, and with a different default from the one that actually routes (0.1)

generate() crashed with a device-side CUDA assert in torch.multinomial on a degenerate distribution -- 4 grid arms (frozvocab, stateq, wt_div, explore) finished training and lost their entire report at the last step

FAB_MIN_STEPS forced off with a local conditional inside forward() left s.min_steps reading 2 while the effective value was 0; the banner, the CHAINING report section and the SAVED CHECKPOINT all read the wrong value, so a resume could rebuild the fabric with a different depth policy
UnboundLocalError: the new module-level _rec helper collided with an existing local `_rec` (recurrent-domain count) inside main()
The [build] DIRTY flag counted untracked files, so a freshly-pulled unmodified checkout reported DIRTY; .gitignore also missed data_pilot/, data_big/, data_grid/

CHAIN_ROUTE was missing from the effective-config table, one commit after the table was introduced to make that impossible -- it switched the entire routing architecture for two pilots and neither log said so
The two config-integrity checks ran at banner time, before the report's own env reads had happened, producing false positives (FAB_CULL_FRAC flagged as unread)
_config_audit() was defined but never called -- the anchor replacement did not match the final print statement
DIV_W was a silent no-op on CHAIN_ROUTE=soc: the soc-loop branch returns before the distinctness term is computed. A full 20-minute pilot (gru6) came back byte-identical to gru4 and measured nothing
Harness: several background verification runs hit the 10-minute Bash timeout (exit 143); `sleep 240` chaining was blocked by the tool and had to be replaced with until-loops
A `cd` leaking into a backgrounded subshell meant three verification arms never ran (rc=2, 'can't open file .../scratchpad/self_organize.py')

Attribution care: several ideas commonly credited to the project originate with CLAUDE, not the researcher, and I have deliberately excluded them from `ideas`: DIV_W=0.05 as an arm (Claude offered it repeatedly, "Your call -- I'd rather not change a default mid-comparison without you saying so"), the ROUTING MIX / CHAIN ORDER / GRADIENT REACH / ROUTER LEARNING / POPULATION CHURN instruments, the ramp latch, the grid design, and the suggestion that "society IS chaining with depth 1" so depth-1 should be the default HALT can extend.

Pattern worth flagging for synthesis: nearly every researcher intervention in this chunk was a course correction that turned out to be right, and each one exposed a class of instrumentation failure rather than a modelling failure. The four classes, in order of discovery: (1) a reported value is WRONG (banner prints env not effective value); (2) a flag is UNREAD (typo trains 20 min on defaults); (3) a flag is READ BUT UNREACHABLE (DIV_W behind an early return); (4) a diagnostic is MEASURED AT THE WRONG SCALE (64-expert toy inverted the 4096-expert answer). Claude's own summary: "That's the third distinct layer of the same failure."

Commit chain in this chunk, in order: b610b89, d7994ea, 30e635d, 7b28570, 8a1e3a7, a5c893a, a71820a, 7e9612d, e0ce4f7, fcdfaa7, ff0f0fa, 09e3d60, 3e67b5d, ffd39b8, 9b179b5, 78c3c1e, 22a708d, 4da76b8, 7b18214, 99ba0f4, b14d60e. All on branch rm-predict.

Remaining suspects named but untested: BAL_WARM decaying load-balance pressure to 0 at step 4000, and per-token loss rising mechanically as minted tokens lengthen (a units artifact).

The researcher's final instruction -- fix any architecture issues, then make the chaining society (CHAIN_ROUTE=soc) the default and run another pilot -- was not completed. The chunk ends mid-investigation with Claude comparing the per-process bits/byte LEARNING CURVE against the per-token LM curve.

DIV_W now runs on both paths and on the soc-loop path but has never produced a measured effect: the toy A/B (socdiv vs socnodiv) gave identical held-out 4.925. No pilot-scale DIV_W measurement exists.
Round-2 grid (vote, vote_w, vote_soc, socloop, socloop_w, society, base, noban, nolatch, ...) was built and pushed but the researcher chose individual pilots instead; it was never run.
Four grid arms (frozvocab, stateq, wt_div, explore) trained fully but lost their entire reports to the generate() CUDA assert; the crash is fixed but those arms were never re-run.

FAB_KEY_NORM=0 was flagged as 'broken rather than a default' after three runs where it was the difference between working and catastrophic (weight-term spread 425 vs region 1.4), but the default was not changed.
q_entry is now untrained (the shared router uses q_route) yet still places newborn keys via seed_key(), so targeted birth uses an untrained projection. Flagged, not decided.
Per-window novelty (surprise is computed per window and averaged away one line before use) was proposed as a cheap fix and never implemented.
VMAX=2048 caps the tokenizer at ~step 21,000 while still minting ~300/interval; raising it costs ~9.4M params on a 3.9M base LM. Named as an untested trade. ENC_CREG also still unruled-on.

CHAIN ORDER on the transition path stays at 0.007-0.058 bits in every arm; only removing the transition matrix (CHAIN_ROUTE=soc) moved it, and that arm predicts worse. The composition question is open.
H(hop1 | hop0, domain) -- whether the chain can vary its second move for the same first move -- was named as the decisive metric at 01:55 and never measured in that conditional form.
The 12-arm smoke gate has not been run since 20:31; all verification since is toy-scale CPU arms, per the researcher's standing instruction.
